filo set FILE... [flags]

  Sets the file_date and the retention of each file, as the retention CSV does,
  for a few files at once: a retention is a period (7y, 18m, 6w, 30d, counted
  from file_date), forever, a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a policy's name. Several
  flags can be given together. keep_until is worked out again.

  All or nothing: if any file cannot be set (a period with no file_date, a
  policy that does not exist, a file missing or not in the register), nothing
  changes and every refusal is listed. It asks only before replacing a value
  already stored, showing what each was and will be; a file given its first
  values is not asked about. A retention set here replaces a policy a directory
  rule set.

Flags
  --file-date DATE         the date a period counts from
  --no-file-date           clear the file_date (refused where a period needs it)
  --retention R            a period, forever, a date or a policy's name
  --no-retention           clear the retention: the files need one again
  --dry-run                show what would change, and change nothing
  -y                       replace values without asking

  A file left past its retention is listed, to check for a typo such as 7d for
  7y; nothing is deleted until filo delete is run.
